utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon, everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could we have appearances for the day, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Dan Saxon for the Prosecution, together with my colleagues Ms. Carmela Javier, Salvatore Cannata, and Mr. Barney Thomas.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon to all. Milos Androvic, Tina Drolec, Daniela Tasic, Novak Lukic, and I'm Gregor Guy-Smith appearing on behalf of Mr. Perisic for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Guy-Smith. Good afternoon to you, Mr. Poje.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just to remind you that you are still bound by the declaration that you made at the beginning of the testimony to tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Before you testified here yesterday, did you have an opportunity to speak with the Prosecutor concerning the testimony you were about to give?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time I met with the Prosecutor was on Saturday.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And when you met with him on Saturday, did you have the opportunity to go over your report as well as your previous testimony in the Martic case?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During this meeting, I reviewed the documents that I prepared in the case of Mr. Martic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Did you have any discussions with the Prosecutor concerning whether or not there was any further documentation that would be of assistance to you with regard to some of the conclusions that you have reached?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. During this proofing session, we only worked with the documents that I had already seen before and that we mentioned yesterday here. So there were no new documents that I received from the Prosecution in my preparation for this testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the information that you had received before, did you at any time during the time that you were compiling your report come across the conclusions of a gentleman by the name of Rade Raseta, chief of security of the SVK Main Staff?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I did not see any document where Mr. Raseta's name was mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Were you aware of the fact during the time that you were compiling your report that there had been a fact-finding commission on the cause and manner of the fall of Western Slovenia - Slavonia, excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only heard about that, but I did not really deal with that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: With regard to the task that you had in terms of your report, you said something -- you said actually two things yesterday, and I want to talk to you about one of them, which is you said -- and I'm referring the Court and counsel to page 3074, lines 14 through lines 20. You were asked the following question, which is: "Now, would you be able to briefly talk the Court through the methodology that you used to prepare the Martic report?" And your response to that was: "Concerning the main question in the report, the main issue, which was who decided on the use of a multiple rocket-launcher Orkan, as I already mentioned, I used literature mentioned earlier from which we can see the following." Now, my question to you, sir, is, when you said that, is it your position as you sit here today that the main issue in the report that you wrote in the Martic case was who decided on the use of the multiple rocket-launcher, Orkan?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I studied the literature and reviewed the documents that I had at my disposal, from the documents one could see that throughout that period Orkan was under the command --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry, that's not my question. My question is a very simple and direct one. Was the main question in the report, the main issue, which was who decided on the use of the multiple rocket-launcher, is your position as you sit here today that that was the main question that you were tasked to deal with in your report, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main question was the consequences of the shelling of Zagreb. That was one question, and the second question was, what establishment did Orkan belong to? So that was the second question, and I had to give a clear answer to those two questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. With regard to what you have just said, when you were asked the question with regard to what your task was in the Martic case, and I'm referring Court and counsel to page 5206, you responded as follows: "I would like -- And it's lines 6 through 18: "I would like to say first and foremost the following; I'd like to tell the Court this first: The subject of my expert report was not to deal with military action from February when the directive was written up until May. What my task and assignment was, that on the basis of the information I was given I should calculate the dispersion pattern during the shelling of Zagreb. So I didn't deal with tactics, operation tactics or the deployment of the units themselves on either side, one or the other side. That was not the task I was given or the assignment I was given. I have read through all the documents, of course. I have all the documents, but it was my task and my assignment that on the basis of the information I had at my disposal to calculate the dispersion pattern during the shelling of the 2nd and 3rd of May, 1995, to determine the dispersion pattern and to see what area is covered by that military operation." Is that what you testified to at that time, sir?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with regard to the report that you have written and has been the subject of some questions here - and I'm referring to section 6.1 - I believe -- which is entitled, if I'm not mistaken: "Who Ordered the Use of an M-87 Orkan VBR." Is that the title of that section?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes: "Who Ordered the Use of an M-87 Orkan VBR."

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Do you think that the matters we discussed yesterday concerning what have been decided as adjudicated facts by this Chamber that Mr. Martic ordered the use of the M-87 Orkan would be of assistance with regard to the conclusion that you drew in this part of your report?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, beg your pardon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt, but I wonder whether we can clarify whether the witness is familiar with the notion of adjudicated facts, which has been referred to in the question of my learned friend at line 20. I'm not aware -- I will check with the witness whether he actually knows the notion of adjudicated fact by a Chamber, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You want to check, or you say you will check?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I will ask that this notion can be checked with the witness, whether he knows what an adjudicated fact is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do you understand the question, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, I understand it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was aware of the judgement through the media, so there is no document that I could show and say that I studied a particular document which speaks of Mr. Martic being the person who had ordered the shelling of Zagreb. I did not have in my possession such a document, no official document, and when I prepared my report at that time, no one really knew that yet, okay?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But sorry, I'm not yet satisfied. I would like to understand from you what you understand the term "adjudicated facts" to mean. I hear what you say about the judgement, but I'm asking about adjudicated facts. What do you understand that concept to mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be honest with you, I don't really know what that is supposed to mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Let me rephrase. You have told us that you were aware of the judgement in Martic; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I read about it in a magazine; I saw a report on TV; I saw it on the internet and so on; but I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And if I understand your testimony, you were contacted after the Martic judgement had been rendered to testify in these proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes. Is the witness aware of when the judgement has been rendered?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The date that the judgement is rendered is irrelevant to the question just asked. The question is whether or not he was contacted after the Martic judgement, meaning after he was aware of the Martic judgement, but I'll rephrase if it's of assistance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: After you read about the Martic judgement, were you contacted by the Prosecution to testify in these proceedings; and by these proceedings, I mean right here, right now, yesterday and today.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, the Prosecution contacted me about 20 days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Okay. Now, yesterday I put some questions to you about whether or not you had particular information regarding Martic ordering the use of the M-87 Orkan rockets. Do you remember me doing that?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And you told us that that was -- for the most part, that was not information that you had at the time that you were drafting your report; correct?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: My question to you is, had you had that information with regard to section 6.1 who ordered the use of an M-87 Orkan VBR, which is the subject matter of your report, would that information have been of assistance to you in making a determination as to who ordered the use of an M-87 Orkan VBR? Just that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, this question has already been asked yesterday. It's one question that has already been asked yesterday. The witness already gave his answer to the same question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you give us a reference, please, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, if I have a minute to go through the transcript, Your Honour. Page 3093, and the exchange is at lines between 20 to 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Yes, I'm reading it. That deals with a different issue. That deals with -- the question is, would that change your analysis at all, sir, and my question here is, would it have been of assistance to you, which is a different question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And what was the question yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The question yesterday was: "With regard to the question or the issue of command and control, had you been supplied with the information that Milan Martic in his capacity as president of Republika Srpska Krajina and supreme commander of the SVK ordered the shelling of Zagreb, would that change your analysis at all, sir, with regard to the issue of command and control?" My question today is, with regard to the issue of the section entitled under 6.1, "Who Ordered the Use of an M-87 Orkan VBR," whether or not the information that Milan Martic had ordered the use of this particular device would have been assistance to him with regard to his analysis in this particular section, that being who ordered, not a question of command or control, but a question of who made the order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Objection overruled.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Had I known earlier that Mr. Martic had ordered the use of Orkan, I would have put it into my report, but since I did not have that information that Mr. Martic had issued that order, I only used the documents that I had at my disposal, such as the directive, orders for reporting, the increasing of combat readiness, where it is explicitly stated that the tasks will be assigned to an organ by the commander of the Main Staff or Colonel Dilas, and that is what I put in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I understand your answer, I understand why you did what you did, and I thank you for your candour, and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any re-examination, Mr. Cannata?

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. One small matter, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Sir, good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: I have one question for you this afternoon. Now, even if the shelling at Zagreb was aiming at military targets, even assuming that, would the Orkan rockets be suitable for firing on targets in a populated area such as Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: JOZEF POJE [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because of blatant errors in the preparation of the initial elements, even if the preparation of the initial elements was complete, because of the great impact dispersion, I think that it was not normal to choose this weapon Orkan as the weapon to shell military targets in Zagreb. I calculated the impact dispersion of Orkan, and my calculation was that it would have been 40 to 45 kilometres, and 1.278 times 1.384 metres, about 1.3 square kilometres, in other words. This means that a part of these rockets would fall or land on targets that are not military targets. They would land in the city itself, and, again, I want to say that if the -- there was the intention to shell Zagreb, the right weapon had not been selected.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. I have no further questions, Your Honour. At this stage, I will tender Mr. Poje's report into evidence, which is 65 ter 4892. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The Defence has no objection to the introduction of Mr. Poje's report exclusive of issues concerning command and control and exclusive of issues of who ordered -- section 6.1, who ordered the firing of the M-87 Orkan for, if no other reason, the very simple reason that the gentleman has told us that had he had that information, he would have included it in his report, and it would have been the basis for his conclusion with regard to a relatively important issue concerning command, control, as well as the actual ordering of this particular device. So with regard to this particular issue and another, we object to the introduction of the report. We are mindful of the Chamber's ruling in this regard as to what weight it will attribute to this particular area, and if the Chamber is inclined to have the report come in in its entirety so as not to hack it up, then we would encourage the Chamber to give these conclusions, once again with regard to the issue of command and control, no weight whatsoever, but that's obviously an argument for another day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. I don't understand why this argument is coming up at this time. The report, then, is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P497.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions, Judge? Thank you very much, Mr. Poje. That brings us to the end of your testimony. I would like to take this opportunity to thank you for taking the time to testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may stand down. Please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cannata.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Thomas will take the next witness, and if I may be excused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You are excused.

utterances.speaker: MR. CANNATA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. The Prosecution calls Mr. Turkovic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I should indicate, Your Honours, that Mr. Turkovic is a 92 ter witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May you please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Thomas, is there a statement by Mr. Turkovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: There are two transcripts from his testimony in the Dragomir Milosevic case, sir. There is reference in those transcripts to previous statements, but it's not intended to tender those as part of his 92 ter package. There are some minor issues of clarification that I can raise with him which would remove the need for those statements to also be admitted into evidence, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I just wanted to know whether we have them or not. That's all. Thank you so much. You may proceed, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, can you start, please, with your full name and your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: My name is Vekaz Turkovic. I was born on the 24th of November, 1972, in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And what is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a computer programmer.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And during the war in Bosnia did you spend time as a crime technician with the Sarajevo Security Services Centre, the CSB?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And related to your time as a crime technician and your duties as a crime technician, did you testify in the case here against Dragomir Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, could we please have 65 ter 09398 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, if you look at the top of that document we can see that it is dated the 25th of April, 2007, and if we could go to --

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if we could go to the next page, please, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And do you recognise that as the commencement of your testimony given in the Dragomir Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity yesterday to review this transcript of your testimony on the 25th of April, 2007?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Is the transcript true and correct?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions today, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honours, if that could please be tendered as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P498.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Madam Registrar. Could we please have 65 ter 09399 on the screen, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, again, we can see that it is dated the 28th of April, 2007.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if we could -- Mr. Usher, I'm sorry, if we could please have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Again, sir, do you recognise that as the continuation of your testimony on the 26th of April, 2007?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Did you have the opportunity yesterday to review the contents of this transcript?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And is it true and correct?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if you were asked the same questions again today, would your answers be the same?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, they would.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Again, if this could please be tendered as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is so admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P499.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Thank you, Madam Registrar. There are three associated exhibits, Your Honour. If they could please also be tendered at this stage. The first is 65 ter 01405, which is referred to in the transcript as Prosecution Exhibit P00603. That's the exhibit number in the Dragomir Milosevic case. I'm sorry, Your Honour. Do we need the other two exhibits at this stage, or does that need to be given an exhibit number before I move on to the other two?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is this the exhibit? You haven't asked about any exhibit to be given exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: First, there are three exhibits referred to within the transcript, but this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sure. I'm waiting for it to come on the screen. Were you not calling it?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The first is 65 ter 01405.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Right. So we're waiting for that --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: On the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, do you recognise that as the official report of the incident that you referred to in your testimony that we have just reviewed, the air-bomb incident of 1 July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Sorry, we might need the next page of the B/C/S, please, Your Honours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I recognise it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. This is the exhibit referred to in the transcripts as Exhibit P00603, and if that could please be tendered in this case as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: 65 ter 01405 is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P500.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Madam Registrar. The next exhibit please, 65 ter number 03307.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, do you recognise this as the forensic investigation report related to the same incident?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. If this -- sorry, this is the exhibit referred to as P00604 in the Dragomir Milosevic testimony. If this could also be tendered as an exhibit in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P501.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Madam Registrar, could we please have Exhibit 65 ter number 01383 on the screen, please. Sorry, 01383B on the screen, please, and if we could scroll through, please, to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, do you recognise these as the photographs you took in relation to this incident?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, these photographs are referred to as Exhibit P00605 in the Dragomir Milosevic testimony. Page 4 of this exhibit has already been tendered in this case as a Prosecution exhibit, so if we could please tender pages 1 to 3 and 5 as a Prosecution exhibit in this case, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: They are so admitted. May they please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P502.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I have a very brief summary of the testimony contained in the admitted transcripts and exhibit, so if I could read that at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. During the war in Bosnia, Mr. Turkovic worked as a crime technician for the Security Services Centre or CSB in Sarajevo. His area of responsibility included Hrasnica, Butmir, Sokolvici Kolonija, and the Igman road. Mr. Turkovic's duties included examining crime scenes and collecting physical evidence. Around 80 per cent of the crime scenes he examined were caused by shelling, sniping, or other wartime activity. Mr. Turkovic investigated the scene of an air-bomb incident which occurred in Bunicki Potok Street, Hrasnica, on 1 July, 1995, and this, Your Honours, is scheduled incident A8. Thirteen people were injured in the incident, two of them seriously. Mr. Turkovic determined that the air-bomb struck one building before ricochetting and exploding on Bunicki Potok Street. He determined the source of fire to be VRS-held territory of Ilidza. And finally, Your Honours, I have just have a few questions by way of clarification and addition relevant to the materials that constitute the 92 ter package.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, firstly, I want to expand a little bit on your background, as it is relevant to your work as an investigator. Were you living in Sarajevo when war broke out in 1992?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: After war broke out, did you join the military police?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And during your time in the military police, did you receive you any training, or did you acquire any experience in investigation?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was trained as a crime scene technician, and the training lasted for six months. I think it was completed in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Just in general terms, can you explain to Their Honours what that training consisted of?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the training consisted in training crime scene technicians how to gather, secure, and transport all evidence from crime scenes as a result of different types of crimes that were committed there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. I'm sorry. I don't understand that answer. "... training consisted in training crime scene technicians how to gather, secure, and" -- oh, I beg your pardon. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: At what stage did you join the civilian police, the CSB?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't remember the date. I can explain the circumstances, but I truly don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: At the time you investigated this air-bomb incident in Hrasnica, had you commenced your work with the CSB?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Do you know or can you give us your best indication of how long you think you had been with the CSB at the time you investigated that incident?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: For a year or two, according to my recollection, but I don't remember exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, what methodology would you adopt when you would arrive to investigate the scene of a shelling such as occurred on 1 July 1995?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is that still background?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: It is still background, but it's obviously now becoming linked to the 1 July incident, Your Honour. So he has tendered a report relating to 1 July, and I just want him to clarify what steps he took to reach the conclusions that appear in that report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And that was not covered in the Milosevic case?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, because they tendered the statement, and it's referred to in the statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is it my turn? Well, mostly when it came to shelling we would immediately proceed with the investigating the crater itself. Most often they hit the ground with shells, so we would analyse craters, and typically we would determine the types of weapons. Normally, there were mostly two types of shells that hit Sarajevo. Some were not of rotational nature, if I may say so. I apologise. Depending on the weapon that launched them, the shells would either rotate as they flew and thus maintain their trajectory and at the end produce a very typical crater that we would call a rose. That was one type of shell. And then there was a different type of shell that didn't rotate but had stabilising wings that would stabilize it during the flight. I apologise. Those are two main categories of shells that landed on Sarajevo. So that was the first item we would determine. Following that, based on the position of the crater and the centre of it, the rose that was produced as a result of the explosion and various shrapnel, based on that, we would establish approximately the direction, the direction from which the shell had arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned a rose. Can you explain to us what that is?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: A crater normally had a rose-like appearance. It was similar to a rose, even though it sounds bizarre, but that's how it looked. So there was a centre of the crater, and then around the crater, since normally shells arrived at an angle, there would be damage produced by shrapnel behind the crater, and that was in the flower-like shape that we called a rose. I can give more details if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Let's get clarification. Does the bomb that has a stabilizer and that doesn't rotate, does it also make a rose?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, of course. Since all shells come at an angle, most shrapnel land behind crater, and in that case the crater is of a different shape. Normally, it's shaped as a letter V, and it's opposite from the direction in which the shell had arrived. The rotating shells produced smaller roses due to the rotation of the shell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Was this the same methodology you applied in your investigation of the 1 July 1995 air-bomb incident in Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on the experience and based on that methodology, yes, but in this case there was no crater, at least not in the final location where the explosion occurred, so we had to do it a bit differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So can you explain to us what you did differently?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, there was very little that was different except that there was no crater. We came across rocket mortars that were under the ground. We tried to find a bomb, but there was no crater, and it seemed as though the bomb had not exploded there. We thought that the unexploded bomb landed in that yard and that there was another one that landed on the house. So we continued digging and failed to find a bomb, even though we dug several metres into the ground. So we concluded that it was that bomb that landed there and that it ricochetted and ended up on the house where it actually exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: In your report, you are able to identify a source of fire. From what are you able to identify a source of fire?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith. I can't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Never mind. I'll let it go.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Thomas.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Based on two ricochets -- we assumed those were ricochets, so based on those two ricochets we were able to establish the trajectory of the bomb, and it indicated approximately the source from which it was launched and the final location where it exploded.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could please have, Your Honours, Exhibit P500 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And the pages I'm looking for are page 3 in both the English and B/C/S versions, the second to last paragraph in the English version and the final paragraph in the B/C/S version. Thank you, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, in the report that we have on the screen, in the third line down of the English version, there is the finding that: "... the projectile had been fired from the aggressor's positions in the north, the surrounding area of Ilidza." I just want to ask you, please, who held those positions? Who is the aggressor in that context?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where are you reading, sir, on this page?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. It's the second-to-last paragraph. It's the sentence that begins: "After the arrival at the site ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, you can see there that the finding is that the projectile had been fired from the aggressor's positions in the north, the surrounding area of Ilidza. My question is, who was the aggressor? Who held those areas? Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: That area was under the control of the Army of Republika Srpska as they were called at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Finally, you've mentioned in your transcript and in these documents certain areas and locations. So that the Trial Chamber when they later consider this material can visualize where you're talking about, I want to just refer you to a map and point out some of these locations, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Your Honours, if we could please have Exhibit P439 on the screen, which is map 8 in the Court binder, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, it's a little bit difficult to see, but you would recognise that as a map of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could have the bottom left-hand quarter enlarged, please, and if we could scroll down a little bit, please, Mr. Usher. Down, please. Thank you. That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: First of all, we've spoken of Hrasnica. Do you see Hrasnica on that map?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly in this area here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm going to ask Mr. Usher to give you an electronic pen so that you can mark the screen for us there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if you could mark that with the number 1, please.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You then spoke of Ilidza being your findings as to source of fire. Could you please mark Ilidza on the map?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And if you could mark that with the number 2, please.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, if that map could please be tendered as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before it is, I would like to know what is the target, if he can show us the target that was hit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Number 1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Number 1 is the target?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. The map is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit P 503.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry. It is 439, isn't it -- oh, yes. 503, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Madam Registrar. And finally, if we could have Exhibit P439 on the screen, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You mention other areas of responsibility in your transcript. I just want to record those for completion on the map, please. The first was Butmir. Do we see Butmir on the map?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you mark that for us, please.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Again, if you could put the number 1 next to that indication.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And the second area with which you were concerned in your area of responsibility was Sokolvici Kolonija. Do we see that area on the map?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could with you mark that area for us, please?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, as number 2. Thank you. And finally, the Igman road, can you draw a line on the Igman Road, where it was within your area of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. The Igman Road goes up Mount Igman, but the most interesting portion of the road was the one close to Hrasnica, so I will only mark that portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If you could mark that number 3.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And if could you just explain to Their Honours why this was the most -- sorry, interesting or important was the word you used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Interesting. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Why was this the most interesting part of the road?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Because that's where most incidents occurred because it was under direct fire from the Army of Republika Srpska from two sides, so most incidents occurred there. Humanitarian convoys were frequently hit and similar incidents. The other hand, on the other side of this part there was no incident, there was no -- there was a fire, I believe, and that's why I said this portion at the foothills is more interesting.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you, Your Honours. If that could please be tendered as a Prosecution exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit P504.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And Mr. Usher, thank you. That completes the assistance that we need from you at this point.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And finally, Mr. Turkovic, was this the first air-bomb incident that you had been involved in?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: It was not the only one, but whether it was the first one, to be frank, I can't recall the date. I don't know if it was the first one, but it wasn't the only one.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: How many air-bomb incidents, air-bombs landing in ABiH-held Sarajevo were you involved in or were aware of?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean how many of them do I know of or how many of them was I directly involved in?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Well, either through your direct involvement or otherwise, how many do you personally know about?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I think about 7 or 8 altogether, approximately.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And which forces, to your knowledge, used air-bombs?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: The Republika Srpska army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Mr. Turkovic, thank you. Those are the questions I have for you at this stage. My learned friends will have some questions for you, if you would kindly wait there. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Thomas. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith. Cross-examination by Guy-Smith:

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: When you received your training in the military police for purposes of becoming a crime scene technician, you studied photography; true?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was part of the course.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Crime scene examination?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, we can't hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Finger-print examination?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You learned to draw scene plans and how to locate and save evidence that was found at the scene; true?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you did do some studies of ballistics and fire-arms; correct?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You also studied the handling of blood samples and blood traces; correct?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With regard to the studies that you did concerning ballistics, how long did you study ballistics in the 6-month course that you took in which you learned all of the subjects that we just talked about?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: We studied ballistics as one subject where what we studied was mechanical traces in general, and I don't know how long this took because we spent quite a lot of time on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And how would you define the study of ballistics? What would you be studying precisely?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I would like to clarify something, if I may. The CSB at the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Excuse me. The question is a simple one. How would you define ballistics, the study of ballistics, since it's something that you've told us you studied. How would you define it?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: As I said, ballistics was studied as part of a course on mechanical traces in general, and this was just gaining some basic knowledge on ballistics, about ballistics, which was not really quite extensive in view of the time that we had at our disposal. So we didn't really possess a lot of knowledge on ballistics, but what we did was collect traces and analyse them.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And with regard to the issue of fire-arms, because you've told us that you did do some studies --

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: -- of ballistics and fire-arms, with regard to your study of fire-arms, what did you study?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the first thing that comes to mind, for instance, was the penetration of a bullet through a material, for instance, through glass; we would learn how to determine the direction from which the bullet was fired. But the final analysis was performed it at the MUP itself, not at the CSB. We were the ones who actually just provided the first opinion, and the experts in MUP gave their own final analysis and opinions.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I apologise. We may have been speaking at cross purposes. It was my understanding that the subjects that you studied you did when you were in the military police; correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the training was held by the MUP, the civilian police, for us members of the military police - there were five of us - and then later on we were transferred to the civilian police.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm just referring for the moment about your military time. We'll speak about your civilian time shortly. But just with regard to your military time, the training that we've been discussing is training you received while you were in the military; true?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it was provided we were trained by the civilian police, and as military policemen we were guests, as it were, there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With regard to your duties after you were trained in the subjects you've outlined here - photography, crime scene examination, finger-print examination, the drawing of scene plans, how to locate and save evidence, and some studies of ballistics and fire-arms, as well as the handling of blood sampling and blood traces - you went back into the military police as an active military police officer; correct?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: While I was in training, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And you became an investigator, and you were responsible for investigating black-marketing, property crimes, and even drug dealing; correct? You have to speak into the microphone; otherwise you don't have --

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] I'm waiting for interpreter.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, crime -- general crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I noticed that you just responded to me in English. You understand English very well, do you not?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And as a matter of fact, you were not only an interpreter for an American company, but you were an interpreter for the United Nations during the war in Sarajevo; is that correct, or was it after the war in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Were you engaged in simultaneous interpretation?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with regard to the issue of black-marketing, you say you investigated black-marketing, could you tell you Chamber what kinds of material you investigated with regard to black-marketing in the military police?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: It was -- they were so-called crimes. Perhaps you find that funny, but that's how it was. For instance, people were arrested because of trading with UNPROFOR even if only an egg was exchanged or some chocolates. So those were the cases, minor or of a greater scope or scale.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Well, after we return from the break, we can discuss those crimes of a greater scale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at 4.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Mr. Guy-Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With regard to those crimes concerning black-marketing that were of a greater scope or scale, did you have occasion to be involved in any investigation of crimes - black-marketing, that is - with regard to the movement of ammunition or guns?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Not that I can remember, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Fuel?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: There were probably cases of trading fuel with UNPROFOR, but to be honest, I can't really recall. There was a lot of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: There was a lot of what, trading fuel with UNPROFOR?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, fuel. Not only with the UNPROFOR, but there were also a lot of thefts of fuel and generally in this whole area of trading fuel.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: When you are referring to thefts of fuel, those are thefts of fuel by military soldiers stealing fuel from the army, or are you talking about something else? Because as I understood your jurisdiction, it was a jurisdiction dealing with the military.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, but frequently, perpetrators were soldiers so that many of those cases were such that they were under our jurisdiction.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With regard to the issue of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the counsel please speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With regard to the issue of black-marketing of ammunition, were you involved in any investigations of black-marketing concerning ammunition with the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that you've already asked this, and my answer is no, not that I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Would it refresh your recollection if I were to tell you that you left the military police in December of 1993 to join the civilian police force? Does that sound right to you?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it doesn't help jog my memory as to ammunition commerce or trading, if that's what you meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Understood. I've moved on. When you left -- when you left the military police and you moved on to the civilian police force, you were, as I understand it, for approximately a year, what I call a street cop. You worked on -- right?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So that would take us to about December of 1994, which is when you joined the centre for public security, the CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And that is the same CSB that you received training from when you were in the military; correct?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: The federal ministry organised the training, but it was in the same institution. In other words, the CSB today is cantonal, and the federal ministry was providing training.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And your function when you joined the CSB was that of a crime technician which is similar to the function that you were trained for in that 6-month training period; correct?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I was trained to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With regard to the issue of locating and saving evidence that was found at the scene, what were you taught in that regard?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: The protection of traces, their transport, and, of course, recovery and study on the spot itself. Nothing specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we -- I'm going to move to another subject. Could we please have P503 up on the screen. We're all waiting now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Looking at the area that you've circled and marked with a number 1, which I understand is the area of Hrasnica?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you please tell us how -- what the distance is that area that you've marked covers?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean the circumference that I drew here or the distance of point 2 to something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I mean the distance that is contained within the circle that you've marked as number 1, and it would be, I think, probably diametre, not the circumference.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I think it's about 1 kilometre, a bit less, maybe. I'm not absolutely certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to have to take this off the screen because each exhibit has its own specialness.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we please have P439, the map, up. And if we could enlarge that area, I'd appreciate it. Great, thank you. And if we could enlarge the general area around -- yes, the bottom left-hand side where the gentleman has identified the area of Hrasnica. If you could make that a bit bigger, please, and maybe a titch bigger if you could do it one more time. I'd appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, with regard to -- I'm going to need the help of the usher. Do you have in your mind's eye the area that you circled.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you just scroll it down a bit, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Looking at that area, there seem to be a fair number of black markings, and looking at the -- about in the middle of the screen, there's some markings that are relatively large that are in black. Do you see those? Are you with me?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know what you are referring to. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If you were to go to the very top of the map, and if you were to go over 1, 2, 3 squares where it says -- 1, 2, 3, 4 squares, the square past the one that says Butmir, and you come directly down 1, 2, 3, 4 squares, there's an area where there are a number of black markings. No, down further and to your right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I'm going to ask the usher if he could erase those other marks at the moment. Thank you, much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With regard to the area that you've just circled there, could you identify what those buildings were, during the time that you were engaged in your investigation in July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know. I think these were some factories, some plants, but I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: When you say factories, plants, but you are not sure, do you recall whether they were operating factories or not?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I think they weren't, but I'm not sure. I think that this is approximately where the line of defence was, but I'm really not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And when you say line of defence, would you be referring to the line of defence between the two armies, that being the ABiH and the VRS?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but I would like to stress that I'm really not certain, but I think it was in that area somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Can you tell us as you are looking at this map and in this general area approximately where the line of defence was? I understand you're really not certain, but can you give us a rough idea of where it was?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: All I can say is that it was approximately in the area of these factories, but I really can't be more specific. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: All right. Could you then perhaps -- then what would be helpful is if you could -- if we could erase this or if you could just draw a circle about the general area of approximation of where the line of defence was, I'd appreciate it, since it will cover both the issue of the factories as well as the line of defence.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I really cannot indicate the line of defence because I really don't know. I think the factory was mentioned when people talked about this thing, where the line of defence was; people discussed this, but I think I really couldn't give you any more specific description.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Very well, then. Just put a circle around the factories.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And mark that with an "F" for factories.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, once again looking at this same map, do you know whether or not in the area that you've marked as an "F" there were any buildings that were inhabited by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Moving over one square to your left, you'll notice that there is in that particular square, among other things, an area that is marked with an oval. Do you know whether or not there were any buildings located in that area that were inhabited or used by the ABiH?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I think that these are residential buildings here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: So your answer would be that you don't know whether or not any buildings in that area were inhabited by the ABiH; correct?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I really don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Once again, could you do me one more favour, which is, do you see that part of the Igman Road that you testified to earlier as being interesting on this particular map? Could you mark that for us, please?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And with regard to -- could you put an -- I'm sorry, could you put an "IG" there for Igman Road?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Thank you. And with regard to the area that you've marked with an "IG" for Igman Road, do you know whether or not there were any positions, military positions of the Bosnian army along that area of the Igman Road that you've marked as being interesting?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I passed through that area a couple of times, and I don't think that there were any significant positions or any buildings or anything of the sort belonging to the army.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You've used the term "significant." How do you define that term, sir?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I was just placing it in the context of your question. I meant to say relevant. That was the context that I placed it in. So one couldn't see any soldiers; one couldn't see any buildings, facilities, or anything of the sort. I would more often come across UNPROFOR in that area than across soldiers of the Bosnian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Thank you. Could we have this admitted as the defendant's next in order, and could we have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D37.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could we have the same fresh map P439 back up on the screen again, and if we could at this point make it a bit smaller so that we can get more of Sarajevo into it. Can we get it a little bit bigger. Great. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, looking at this particular map, while you were in the military police, could you put an "X" on the map as to where your military police headquarters were?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please zoom into the area that I show so that I can draw in the location with more precision. It will be easier for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Could we -- what's going to happen is your circle is going to go away, and we're going to have to do it again because every time we move the map, it goes away, but I'm happy to do that. If we could zoom in, then, I'd appreciate it. Is that better, or do you need it larger? You want it a little larger?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Depends on how accurate do you need the "X" to be.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'd like it to be accurate. I think the Chamber needs accuracy here.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please zoom into this area, this here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Is that of help?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you mark now just with an "X" where the military police headquarters were.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please give me a bit more time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Absolutely. Take all the time you need.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: If I recognise the bridges accurately, then I think it was here.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Could you put by that "X" the letters "MP" for military police?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. With the map in this condition, looking at the balance of the area that's on that map, can you identify for us -- well, let me ask you another question before that. In terms of being in the military police, was your area of responsibility the city of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Theoretically speaking, no. Practically speaking, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And with regard to your area of responsibility, practically speaking being yes, considering that you were in the military police, did you have among other facts available to you the location of units of your army that were stationed in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, not as a member of the military police. Those things were common knowledge. People within the city knew them. Practically everybody knew everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. That probably made your job easier in a certain sense. Looking at this part of the map that we have up there, can you identify for us any areas on this part of the map that were areas where your army had units stationed?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I could draw in the lines approximately, but as for barracks or any other military facilities, not really. Perhaps I could remember one or two of them, but not more, especially not in this part of the city. Perhaps more to the west I could remember about two barracks, but not more than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: With regard to this area, are there lines that you could draw in approximately, understanding that, of course, it is an approximation as to where units were?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Let's say that this would roughly be the southern line.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And could you mark that with an "ABiH"?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And going north -- north of where the military police headquarters were -- are indicated, were there any units of the ABiH stationed in that area?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: That's the part I'm least familiar with in the entire town. I know the least about that particular part of the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And so I take it, then, you would not be comfortable in drawing any lines north of your military police headquarters?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, truly not.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: That's absolutely fair. With regard to the area north of your military police headquarters, were you aware, without knowing precisely where they were, that there were units of the ABiH in that area.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: You'd have to be more specific as to "that area." What does that mean? To the north, yes, but how far?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: I'm referring to the north and only to what is contained on the map that you see before you right now, nothing further than that. I'm not asking you to go outside the four corners of this particular map because that wouldn't, among other things, be fair.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Well, if you're asking me about the military facilities, I really don't know anything about this. I'm not familiar with that area. There was no need for me to come there, to work there. I know roughly where the line could have been, but I don't know anything about the facilities there.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. And when you say you know "roughly where the line could have been," does this -- could you draw roughly where the line could have been on the map as it's presently constituted?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: From the north, that line was further from the centre of the city, so I will draw it in somewhat further, but to say that I remember this with any accuracy, no. Roughly something like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Understood. That's understood. And just for purposes of the record, you have continued the line that was previously put forth with "ABiH" on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could we have this marked as Defendant's next in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Could we have P439 up on the screen again, and I'm sorry for having taken that off.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: One final question with regard to the areas that you had drawn that were -- and I understood once again that it's not definite, but areas where approximations of the ABiH were. Did that change after you left the military police in 1993? Is that a fair representation of the area for 1994 and 1995 when you were involved in the civilian police?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the lines?

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, roughly, that's what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: We are back at the master map again, and we've dealt with one area. Looking at the master map now, are there other areas where you are aware there were ABiH units stationed or location -- stationed or located? And I'm leaving the map small for the moment because I don't know whether or not you're going to want to enlarge any particular areas or not.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: So the troops were everywhere where the lines were. You know about all my reservations about how accurate I can be about -- how accurate I can be about all of that, and there were some facilities within the lines, not right next to the lines, but more towards the city, but, yes, there were some that were close to the lines that occur to me right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Should we leave the map in this particular iteration, or should we change the size of it, make it bigger or smaller? Whatever works for you for the purposes of including those areas.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Could we increase the useful area, so we don't need to see the corners that are of not much use.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. Would you like it bigger again?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: No, this is perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Okay. And if you could engage in the same exercise that you'd engaged in with the last exhibit in terms of the other areas where there were ABiH units - to your best approximation, understood - I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I can't be specific about this part here. I can't be specific about any part, but this would roughly be how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And could you mark the line that's on the top with "ABiH 2"?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. Let me just say something. I see something that's quite inaccurate; that's this line here. It was more to the west. In case if it's important, I can redraw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: You mean the line you just drew?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Oh, well, let's do that. Please, let's do that.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [In English] Just this part, please. Thank you. [Interpretation] This is a bit more accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: If we could have that marked with "ABiH," and just put the number "2" after that, and for the bottom line, "ABiH 3."

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: And could we have this marked as Defendant's next in order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May it please be marked, as it is admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D39.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: The report -- I'm moving to another subject now. The report that was made in this particular case, did you sign that report?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. When it comes to the report of the crime technician, then, yes, I signed that one. There were two normally -- two reports normally, and I signed the report of the crime technician examining the scene.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And by that, I take it you are referring to -- that would be --

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: If we could have up on the screen P500. You know what, I lied. I don't want that. I want P501.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, with regard to this report, you indicated that the offence was committed -- and I'm referring to paragraph 4 in the English, the first paragraph, you state: "The missile first hit the wall of a house owned by Alija Kustura ..." and you give an address number. "Then the ground and the yard of this house ricochetted and exploded at Bunicki Potok Street hitting the next house." Right?

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the issue of the trajectory of this particular missile, were you able to determine what was the angle of deflection after it hit the first house? Because you mentioned there was a ricochet, so there's some angle.

utterances.speaker: VEKAZ TURKOVIC
utterances.text: Now, you are really asking me a lot. I wouldn't be able to say exactly what the angle was. I couldn't even say what it was roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: And since it ricochetted -- as I understand it, it ricochetted twice from what I understand, that would mean that after it ricochetted the first time and there was some angle of deflection, whatever it may be, when it hit the second time and ricochetted, then there would be a second angle of deflection, correct, of some nature?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, where do we have it that it ricochetted twice?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: In his testimony. Page 46. Thank you. Line 22 -- I'm sorry, page 22, line 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Page?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: 22, line 25. In response to a question asked by Mr. Thomas at page 22, line 18: "In your report, you were able to identify the source of fire. From what are you able to identify as a source of fire?" "A. Based on two ricochets -- we assumed those were ricochets, based on those two ricochets, we..." something, "... the trajectory of the bomb, and it indicated the source at which it was launched and the final location where it exploded."
